recap.back_html: What decision will this inform, who makes it, and when?
If the answer were A, what would you do? And if B? If both lead to the same action, the analysis changes nothing.
Talk about their work, not your idea. Ask about specific past events, not future opinions. Talk less, listen more.
Compliments, fluff (generic or hypothetical answers) and feature requests that hide a motive.
recap.front_html: Three kinds of bad interview data

lessons.takeaway_html: Ask what decision a request serves, who makes it and when. Interview about specific past events, filter out compliments, fluff and feature requests, and confirm a written brief.
lessons.title: Find the decision behind the request

recap.back_html: High power and interest: manage closely. High power, low interest: keep satisfied. Low power, high interest: keep informed. Low both: monitor.
Each person's stance (supporter, neutral or opponent), what they care about, what you need from them, the channel and how often.

recap.back_html: At the start of each phase and after any event that changes someone's power or interest, such as an audit.

lessons.takeaway_html: Score each stakeholder on power and interest, note their stance, and choose an approach per quadrant: manage closely, keep satisfied, keep informed or monitor. Review the map at each phase.
lessons.title: Map your stakeholders by power and interest

recap.back_html: Trade what the other person values for what you need. It rests on reciprocity.
Inspiration, task, position, relationship and personal.
Assume an ally, clarify your goals, diagnose their world, identify currencies, deal with the relationship, give and take.
A negative currency. Use it last, because it costs the relationship.

lessons.takeaway_html: Diagnose what the other person values, offer currencies they care about, such as task help or visibility, and trade for what you need. Keep escalation for the last resort.
